'''''Phylica''''' is a genus of [[plant]]s in the family [[Rhamnaceae]]. It contains about 150 species,<ref name="Richardson2003">{{cite journal |author1=James E. Richardson |author2=Michael F. Fay |author3=Quentin C. B. Cronk |author4=Mark W. Chase |year=2003 |title=Species delimitation and the origin of populations in island representatives of ''Phylica'' (Rhamnaceae) |journal=[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]] |volume=57 |issue=4 |pages=816–827 |jstor=3094618 |doi=10.1554/0014-3820(2003)057[0816:SDATOO]2.0.CO;2 |pmid=12778551}}</ref> the majority of which are restricted to [[South Africa]], where they form part of the ''{{lang|af|[[fynbos]]}}''.<ref>{{cite journal |author1=James E. Richardson |author2=Frans M. Weitz |author3=Michael F. Fay |author4=Quentin C. B. Cronk |author5=H. Peter Linder |author6=Gail Reeves |author7=Mark W. Chase |year=2001 |title=Phylogenetic analysis of ''Phylica'' L. (Rhamnaceae) with an emphasis on island species: evidence from plastid ''trnL-F'' and nuclear internal transcribed spacer (ribosomal) DNA sequences |journal=[[Taxon (journal)|Taxon]] |volume=50 |issue=2|pages=405–427 |jstor=1223889 |doi=10.2307/1223889}}</ref> A few species occur in other parts of [[southern Africa]], and on islands including [[Madagascar]], the [[Mascarene Islands]], [[Île Amsterdam]], [[Saint Helena]], [[Tristan da Cunha]],<ref name="Richardson2003" /> and [[Gough Island]]. ''Phylica piloburmensis'' from the [[Burmese amber]] of Myanmar, dating to around 99 million years ago during the mid-[[Cretaceous]], was originally described as the oldest fossil member of the genus,<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Shi |first1=Chao |last2=Wang |first2=Shuo |last3=Cai |first3=Hao-hong |last4=Zhang |first4=Hong-rui |last5=Long |first5=Xiao-xuan |last6=Tihelka |first6=Erik |last7=Song |first7=Wei-cai |last8=Feng |first8=Qi |last9=Jiang |first9=Ri-xin |last10=Cai |first10=Chen-yang |last11=Lombard |first11=Natasha |date=2022-01-31 |title=Fire-prone Rhamnaceae with South African affinities in Cretaceous Myanmar amber |url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1038/s41477-021-01091-w |journal=Nature Plants |volume=8 |issue=2 |pages=125–135 |doi=10.1038/s41477-021-01091-w |pmid=35102275 |s2cid=246443363 |issn=2055-0278|url-access=subscription }}</ref> but subsequent studies contested its assignment to the genus ''Phylica<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Oskolski |first1=Alexei A. |last2=Morris |first2=Benjamin B. |last3=Severova |first3=Elena E. |last4=Sokoloff |first4=Dmitry D. |year=2024 |title=Flowers from Myanmar amber confirm the Cretaceous age of Rhamnaceae but not of the extant genus ''Phylica'' |journal=Nature Plants |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=219–222 |doi=10.1038/s41477-023-01591-x |pmid=38278949|bibcode=2024NatPl..10..219O }}</ref>'' and even to the family Rhamnaceae,<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Beurel |first1=Simon |last2=Bachelier |first2=Julien B. |last3=Schmidt |first3=Alexander R. |last4=Sadowski |first4=Eva-Maria |year=2024 |title=Novel three-dimensional reconstructions of presumed ''Phylica'' (Rhamnaceae) from Cretaceous amber suggest Lauralean affinities |journal=Nature Plants |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=223–227 |doi=10.1038/s41477-023-01592-w |pmid=38278948|bibcode=2024NatPl..10..223B }}</ref> with one study placing it in the separate genus ''Nothophylica.''<ref name=":0" />

The genus name ''Phylica'' comes from the Greek φυλλικός (''phullikόs'') "of leaves, concerning leaves", as the stems are densely leafy in most of the species.<ref>{{cite web |last= Notten |first= Alice |date= April 2007 |title= Phylica ericoides |url= https://pza.sanbi.org/phylica-ericoides |website= PlantZAfrica |location= Pretoria |publisher= SANBI |access-date= 12 July 2025}}</ref>
